concepts.name: Outstanding Universal Value (OUV): Definition and Legal Standing
key_dimensions: OUV as the foundational threshold — all 10 criteria are subordinate to it
Three-part test: meeting at least one criterion + integrity + authenticity
UPSC trap: OUV is NOT the criterion itself but the overarching benchmark
Distinction between OUV statement and the nomination dossier

concepts.name: The 10 Criteria Framework: Cultural (i–vi) vs Natural (vii–x) Split
key_dimensions: Criteria i–vi: cultural/civilizational significance (masterpiece, interchange, testimony, typology, association)
Criteria vii–x: natural significance (aesthetic, geological, ecological, biodiversity)
UPSC trap: 'mixed sites' satisfy BOTH cultural and natural criteria simultaneously — not a separate category of criteria
Historical context: originally two separate lists merged in 2005 into unified 10-point system

concepts.name: Criterion (i): Human Creative Genius as a Masterpiece
key_dimensions: Represents 'a masterpiece of human creative genius' — highest artistic/architectural bar
Indian sites inscribed under Criterion i: Taj Mahal, Qutb Minar complex, Red Fort
UPSC trap: not every architectural site qualifies — must demonstrate superlative creative achievement
Distinction from Criterion ii (influence) — Criterion i is about the work itself, not its impact

concepts.name: Criterion (ii): Interchange of Human Values Across Cultures/Time
key_dimensions: Demonstrates important interchange of human values over a span of time or within a cultural area
Focus on cross-cultural diffusion, trade routes, pilgrimage paths — e.g., Great Himalayan National Park indirectly; more relevantly Hampi
UPSC trap: Criterion ii requires evidence of EXCHANGE, not mere excellence — often confused with Criterion i
Silk Road nominations and serial transnational nominations frequently use this criterion

concepts.name: Criterion (iii): Unique or Exceptional Testimony to a Civilization or Cultural Tradition
key_dimensions: Bears unique or exceptional testimony to a cultural tradition or civilization that is living, disappeared, or at risk
Key word: 'testimony' — documentary or physical evidence of a culture, not just aesthetic value
Indian relevance: Buddhist monuments at Sanchi, Elephanta Caves
UPSC trap: a 'disappeared civilization' site qualifies — does NOT require the tradition to be living

concepts.name: Criterion (iv): Outstanding Example of Architectural/Technological Ensemble or Landscape
key_dimensions: Represents an outstanding example of a type of building, architectural or technological ensemble illustrating significant stages in human history
Broadest architectural criterion — covers typologies (forts, step-wells, temples) not just individual genius
Indian sites: Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram, Champaner-Pavagadh
UPSC trap: Criterion iv is about 'type/ensemble' while Criterion i is about singular masterpiece — frequently confused

concepts.name: Criterion (v): Outstanding Example of Traditional Human Settlement or Land-Use
key_dimensions: Represents an outstanding example of traditional human settlement, land-use, or sea-use which is representative of a culture — especially when it has become vulnerable under the impact of irreversible change
Vulnerability/threat clause is embedded within this criterion — unique among the 10
Relevance to living heritage: Khajuraho, historic cities with still-inhabited precincts
UPSC trap: Criterion v explicitly mentions vulnerability — this is NOT only an integrity issue but part of the criterion's own logic

concepts.name: Criterion (vi): Association with Living Traditions, Ideas, or Beliefs of Universal Significance
key_dimensions: Directly or tangibly associated with events or living traditions, ideas, beliefs, or works of outstanding universal significance
Operational Guidelines warning: Criterion vi should NOT be the sole basis for inscription — must be combined with other criteria
UPSC trap: This is the ONLY criterion with an explicit advisory against sole application
Indian relevance: Buddhist sites (Bodh Gaya inscribed partly under vi), sites with living pilgrimage traditions

concepts.name: Criterion (vii): Superlative Natural Phenomena or Exceptional Natural Beauty
key_dimensions: Contains superlative natural phenomena or areas of exceptional natural beauty and aesthetic importance
Most subjective of the natural criteria — 'aesthetic beauty' is difficult to benchmark
Indian sites: Kaziranga, Manas, Sundarbans qualify partly on aesthetic/natural spectacle grounds
UPSC trap: beauty alone is insufficient — must be 'superlative' or 'exceptional,' not merely scenic

concepts.name: Criterion (viii): Outstanding Examples of Earth's History and Geological Processes
key_dimensions: Outstanding examples representing major stages of Earth's history, including the record of life, significant ongoing geological processes, or significant geomorphic or physiographic features
Covers fossil records, volcanic landscapes, karst formations, canyon systems
Indian context: Western Ghats inscription partly uses criterion x but geological uniqueness is relevant
UPSC trap: Criterion viii is about Earth's HISTORY (past processes) while Criterion ix is about ONGOING ecological/biological processes

concepts.name: Criterion (ix): Outstanding Examples of Ongoing Ecological and Biological Processes
key_dimensions: Outstanding examples representing significant ongoing ecological and biological processes in the evolution of terrestrial, freshwater, coastal and marine ecosystems
Keyword: 'ongoing' — must demonstrate active, dynamic ecological processes, not just biodiversity stock
Indian sites: Western Ghats, Great Himalayan National Park inscribed under this criterion
UPSC trap: Criterion ix ≠ Criterion x — ix is about processes/evolution of ecosystems; x is about species diversity and threatened species

concepts.name: Criterion (x): Biodiversity Conservation and Threatened Species
key_dimensions: Contains the most important and significant natural habitats for in-situ conservation of biological diversity, including those containing threatened species of outstanding universal value
Only criterion explicitly mentioning IUCN Red List — 'threatened species of outstanding universal value'
Indian sites: Kaziranga (one-horned rhino), Manas (golden langur, pygmy hog), Sundarbans (Bengal tiger)
UPSC trap: Criterion x requires in-situ conservation significance — ex-situ conservation (zoos) does NOT qualify

concepts.name: Integrity Condition: Scope, Wholeness, and Intactness
key_dimensions: Integrity assesses whether the property includes all elements necessary to express OUV and is of adequate size
Three sub-tests: wholeness (all necessary elements present), intactness (no deterioration), adequate size
Different integrity tests apply to natural vs cultural sites — visual integrity, structural integrity, functional integrity
UPSC trap: Integrity is a CONDITION of inscription, not one of the 10 criteria — must be met alongside criteria, not instead of them

concepts.name: Authenticity Condition: Applies Only to Cultural Sites
key_dimensions: Authenticity tests whether cultural properties express OUV through authentic attributes: form, design, materials, substance, use, function, traditions, spirit
Nara Document on Authenticity (1994) — broadened authenticity beyond material substance to include intangible dimensions
UPSC trap: Authenticity is NOT required for natural sites — it is exclusively a condition for cultural and mixed sites
Reconstruction debate: heavily reconstructed sites may fail authenticity test (e.g., controversies around rebuilt structures)

concepts.name: Mixed Sites: Satisfying Both Cultural and Natural Criteria
key_dimensions: Mixed sites must meet at least one cultural criterion (i–vi) AND at least one natural criterion (vii–x)
Globally rare category — only about 39 mixed sites worldwide as of 2023
Indian mixed site: Khangchendzonga National Park (inscribed 2016) — first Indian site under 'cultural landscape' and mixed category
UPSC trap: 'Mixed' does NOT mean moderate cultural + moderate natural — it requires independently satisfying OUV on BOTH cultural AND natural grounds

concepts.name: Cultural Landscapes: A Subcategory Under Cultural Criteria
key_dimensions: Cultural landscapes represent combined works of nature and humankind — recognized as a distinct typology within cultural criteria, not a separate criterion
Three types: designed landscape (intentional), organically evolved landscape (relict or continuing), associative cultural landscape
Khangchendzonga National Park: India's first 'associative cultural landscape' — based on community beliefs and spiritual associations, not physical design
UPSC trap: Cultural landscapes are inscribed under cultural criteria (especially v and vi), NOT as a separate 11th criterion

concepts.name: Serial and Transnational Nominations: Implications for Criteria Application
key_dimensions: Serial nominations group multiple component sites under a single inscription — each component need not individually meet all criteria but collectively must demonstrate OUV
Transnational serial sites span multiple countries — require joint management plans
Indian example: Victorian Gothic and Art Deco Ensembles of Mumbai (serial nomination within one city)
UPSC trap: In serial nominations, OUV is assessed for the SERIES as a whole — individual components may be unimpressive in isolation

concepts.name: UNESCO's Advisory Bodies: ICOMOS vs IUCN and Their Role in Criteria Evaluation
key_dimensions: ICOMOS (International Council on Monuments and Sites) evaluates cultural nominations (criteria i–vi)
IUCN (International Union for Conservation of Nature) evaluates natural nominations (criteria vii–x)
Both bodies conduct field evaluations and submit recommendations to World Heritage Committee — Inscribe / Refer / Defer / Not inscribe
UPSC trap: The World Heritage Committee makes the FINAL decision — it can override advisory body recommendations (has done so for political reasons)

concepts.name: The Tentative List: Mandatory Precondition for Nomination
key_dimensions: A property CANNOT be nominated unless it first appears on a State Party's Tentative List for at least one year
India's Tentative List currently contains 52 properties (as of 2023) — knowledge of which properties are on it vs already inscribed is a UPSC trap area
Tentative listing does not guarantee inscription — many properties remain listed for decades
UPSC trap: Being on the Tentative List is a procedural prerequisite, NOT an indicator of meeting the OUV criteria

concepts.name: World Heritage in Danger List: Criteria for Listing and Delisting
key_dimensions: A site is placed on the Danger List when it faces specific/potential threats to its OUV, integrity, or authenticity — can be ascertained or potential danger
Listing triggers international assistance and attention — NOT a punitive measure
Delisting (removal from WHL entirely) is extremely rare: only Dresden Elbe Valley (2009) and Arabian Oryx Sanctuary (2007) have been delisted
UPSC trap: Danger listing ≠ delisting — danger listing is a conservation tool; delisting requires that OUV has been irreversibly lost and is a separate, more drastic step
